requirements.evidence: The pieces exist (CreateQueue.php:17, UpdateQueue.php:15, SetQueueAccess.php:17, QueuePermission.php:5-8, QueueAccess.php:11-31, migration:11-23, QueuePolicy.php:12-56), but authorization cannot run: UserRole is never imported in the new policy (QueuePolicy.php:20,27,40), create() takes an array where Gate passes the Entity (QueuePolicy.php:16-18), Ticket::call authorizes after the LogicException (Ticket.php:98-100), the factory creates membership and queue in different entities (QueueAccessFactory.php:21-24), duplicate handling is MySQL-only (CreateQueue.php:44-51, UpdateQueue.php:47-53), and the required docs are absent.

conventions.evidence: Good: domain writes live in Actions and authorize inside them (CreateQueue.php:20, UpdateQueue.php:18, SetQueueAccess.php:20) and the migration has a reversible down() (migration:26-29). Bad: no tests at all (violates the project's TDD rule), docs are not kept in sync (docs/business-rules.md, docs/database-schema.md, CHANGELOG.md absent from the diff), and app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:7 extends a non-existent base class and is dead code.

security.evidence: Every write path goes through Gate::authorize (CreateQueue.php:20, UpdateQueue.php:18, SetQueueAccess.php:20) and inputs are validated server-side; however the audit actor is read from auth()->id() instead of the authorized $actor (SetQueueAccess.php:47,58) and the LIKE-based permission lookup (QueuePolicy.php:51-54) can match corrupted non-array JSON, contrary to the required deny rule.

tests.evidence: The whole change.diff adds only app/, database/ and docs-less files; there is no tests/ file and no Pest/PHPUnit test for any of the new actions, the policy, the model, the factory or the authorization paths.

simplicity.evidence: Some duplication and dead weight: identical QueryException/1062 handling in CreateQueue.php:44-52 and UpdateQueue.php:47-54, a single-insert DB::transaction at CreateQueue.php:36-43, an unneeded provider (AuthServiceProvider.php), and unused imports (CreateQueue.php:10 Log, QueuePolicy.php:6 EntityMembership).

readability.evidence: Action classes are small and names are clear, but there is a misleading '// Assuming unique constraint violation' at CreateQueue.php:45, an unused $access at SetQueueAccess.php:53, inconsistent operator spacing (SetQueueAccess.php:30-32), and a dead provider file.

scope.evidence: All new files relate to the requested domain slice; the only extra is the unrequested and unused app/Providers/AuthServiceProvider.php:9-19. No unrelated refactors or UI work.

issues.explanation: UserRole is used but never imported (the file imports only QueuePermission, EntityMembership, Queue, QueueAccess, User and HandlesAuthorization), so it resolves to App\Policies\UserRole and every policy ability that runs (create, update, manageAccess, call) throws a fatal Error.

create(User $user, array $parameters) has the wrong contract: Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('create', [Queue::class, $entity]) removes the class name and passes the Entity as the second argument, so the array type hint raises a TypeError instead of authorizing.

The 'call' gate is checked after the 'Only waiting tickets can be called' LogicException, so an already-called ticket throws LogicException rather than AuthorizationException; the task explicitly requires authorize before the waiting-ticket check, even for already-called tickets.

The audit context uses auth()->id() instead of the passed $actor->id, so when the action is invoked for an authorized manager without that user being the session user (e.g. jobs/tests/CLI) actor_id is null or wrong, violating the required 'the manager's user id' contract.

Employee 'call' access is decided with a SQL LIKE '%"call"%' on the JSON column instead of casting permissions to an array and checking it contains 'call'; a corrupted non-array value such as {"call":true} or "call" would match and grant access, which the task says must deny.

Membership and queue are created from independent factories, so the default row links two different entities; the contract requires QueueAccess::factory() to create a membership and queue that belong to the same entity (the comment acknowledges the gap).

Duplicate-slug detection only handles MySQL error code 1062 and indexes $e->errorInfo[1] unconditionally, so on SQLite/PostgreSQL (or when errorInfo is null) a unique-index violation surfaces as a raw QueryException instead of the required ValidationException.

No Pest/PHPUnit tests ship with the new actions, policy, model, factory or the two call paths, so validation, authorization, duplicate-slug, revoke/no-log and cross-entity cases are entirely unverified.
The task explicitly requires updating all three docs, but none of them (nor any docs file) appears in the diff, so the queue_access schema and new rules/changelog entry are undocumented.

Every permission entry is cast with (string) before validation, so non-string entries are not rejected as the task requires; an object/Stringable that stringifies to 'call' is accepted and an array entry triggers an 'Array to string conversion' warning instead of a ValidationException.

It extends Illuminate\Foundation\Providers\AuthServiceProvider, which is not the framework's policy provider base (Support\Providers\AuthServiceProvider), is not registered in bootstrap/providers.php, and duplicates Laravel's automatic policy discovery, making it dead (and fatal if ever registered) code.

An explicit slug that slugifies to an empty string (e.g. '!!!') is stored without any validation, so queues can be created or renamed with an empty slug, which breaks the uniqueness/identifier expectations of the feature.
Unused Log and EntityMembership imports plus an unused $access variable are leftover noise from the implementation.
The factory class uses the model-side HasFactory trait, which serves no purpose there and is inconsistent with sibling factories.

review.summary: The change adds the queue create/update/access actions, the QueueAccess model, migration and factory, a QueuePermission enum and a QueuePolicy, and wires authorization into CallNextTicket and Ticket::call. It cannot be approved: the policy crashes on an unresolved UserRole class, create has the wrong signature, Ticket::call authorizes after the waiting-ticket check, the audit actor comes from auth() instead of the passed actor, duplicate slugs are only handled for MySQL, the factory creates cross-entity rows, and there are no tests or docs updates.
